product.short: Python capability compiler for static discovery, scientific experiment tracking and typed REST/MCP interfaces with governed execution.
product.standard: OuterSpace Apizr is a Python capability compiler for static discovery and scientific experiment tracking. Inspect Python code and notebooks, record and compare experiment Runs, and expose selected capabilities through typed REST or MCP interfaces. Capture reproducible evidence where supported by the workflow. Governed execution applies explicit policies and controls; reproducibility depends on retained inputs, dependencies and environment support.
product.detailed:
OuterSpace Apizr is an open-source Python capability compiler. It discovers capabilities statically, inspects scripts and notebooks, and helps users choose which functions to expose through typed REST and MCP interfaces. Static discovery reads source without executing application functions. Generated services execute selected functions when clients call them.

Apizr also supports scientific experiment tracking through explicit Python SDK instrumentation and Jupyter session capture. Users can retain parameters, inputs, metrics, artifacts and results, browse experiment Runs, compare their evidence, and prepare supported prediction services from selected recorded results. Reproducible evidence is available where the workflow can capture and retain the required inputs, dependencies and environment information. Recording a Run alone does not guarantee that every computation can be reproduced.

The optional local stdio MCP analysis server is distinct from generated application MCP servers. Its six default tools are apizr_analyze, apizr_readiness, apizr_plan_exposure, apizr_experiment_list, apizr_experiment_show and apizr_experiment_diff. Source analysis requires source.analyze authority; experiment history requires history.read. The optional apizr_delivery_status, apizr_delivery_run and apizr_delivery_resume tools have separate configuration and permission requirements.

Governed execution uses explicit policies, selected execution modes and supported controls. It is not a universal sandbox for arbitrary code. Operators remain responsible for the code, dependencies, permissions and deployment environment they select. Apizr 0.4.6 supports Python 3.11–3.15 on macOS and Linux and is licensed under GPL-3.0-or-later.

analysis_server.registry: Local stdio MCP: Python analysis, readiness, exposure plans and experiment history/comparison.
analysis_server.short: Local stdio MCP server for Python static discovery, readiness, exposure planning and experiment history; delivery requires separate permissions.
analysis_server.standard: The optional OuterSpace Apizr analysis server connects MCP clients to a selected local Python project over stdio. Six default tools cover static discovery, readiness, exposure planning and experiment history/comparison, subject to operator grants. Three delivery tools require separate enablement and permissions. Configure the project, operator policy and activated plugin directory before connecting. Generated application MCP servers are separate interfaces that execute selected functions.
